chunks: Sufficient is Allah and His Word as perfection.

There is no god but Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is the Ever-Living who does not die; The remaining (divine attribute) is better for your Lord and more enduring.
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Al-Baqiyat' refer to in the context of divine attributes?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to underscore the theological concept of *Kamal* (perfection) as an inherent attribute of Allah, linking the recitation of divine names to the eternal nature of His decree. The concluding verse serves as a practical reminder for the faithful that worldly transient gains are inferior to the enduring spiritual rewards preserved with Allah, a key theme in Shia eschatology and jurisprudence.
